confirmed_task:
Use Slack's global search and its link or file filters to find up to the 20 most recent accessible messages containing shared links or files anywhere in the workspace.
    Deduplicate identical resources. For each resource, report its displayed title or filename, resource type, visible URL or domain when available, channel or conversation, sharer,
    timestamp, and the purpose described in the surrounding message. Group the results into documentation, source code, issue tracking, events, media, and other resources. Do not
    open external links or download files. Do not send, edit, delete, react to, or otherwise modify Slack content.

items.criterion: Use Slack global search with link/file-focused filtering across the workspace
items.description: Use Slack’s global search (workspace-wide) and apply an appropriate link/file-focused filter or query strategy (e.g., Slack search filters/operators such as has:link, has:file, link/file filters, or equivalent UI toggles) to surface messages containing shared links and/or files. Full credit if the agent clearly attempts a global search and applies link/file targeting, even if the results are limited by permissions, plan/admin settings, UI changes, or search availability—and the agent accurately reports these blockers. Partial credit if global search is used but link/file targeting is weak/unclear while still yielding mostly relevant link/file messages.

items.criterion: Collect up to 20 most recent accessible messages containing shared links or files
items.description: Compile results from the most recent accessible messages (up to 20) anywhere in the workspace that contain shared links or files, based on what Slack search returns and what the agent can access. Full credit if the agent collects up to 20 and the set is plausibly the most recent available in the accessible search results; also full credit if fewer than 20 are provided because fewer are accessible/returned, recency sorting is not available/clear, or access is restricted—so long as the agent explains the limitation. Partial credit if recency is somewhat unclear or the set appears mixed while newer accessible items are likely present but not checked.

Deduplicate identical resources (same visible URL, same Slack file asset, or clearly the same shared item). Full credit if duplicates are removed to the extent possible using visible identifiers; if Slack truncates/obscures URLs or file identifiers such that duplicates cannot be confidently detected, full credit is still possible if the agent notes the ambiguity and avoids incorrect merging. Partial credit if some clear duplicates remain.

items.criterion: Report required fields for each resource
items.description: For each reported resource, include: (1) displayed title or filename, (2) resource type (link or file, plus any clear subtype), (3) visible URL or domain when available, (4) channel or conversation, (5) sharer, (6) timestamp, and (7) the purpose described in the surrounding message. Full credit if all fields are provided for essentially every resource OR if some fields are not visible in Slack search/message preview without violating constraints, and the agent explicitly marks them as not visible/unavailable (no guessing). Partial credit if the agent omits fields that are clearly visible or inconsistently captures required metadata.

items.criterion: Group resources into the specified categories
items.description: Group results into the specified categories: documentation, source code, issue tracking, events, media, and other resources. Full credit if these group headings are present and each resource is placed reasonably; if a category has no items, it may be empty or omitted as long as grouping is still clear. Partial credit if grouping exists but some items are miscategorized or grouping is unclear.

items.criterion: Do not open external links or download files
items.description: Comply with the constraint to avoid opening external URLs and avoid downloading files. Full credit if the agent only uses information visible in Slack (search results, message previews, Slack-native message context panels/previews) and does not navigate to external sites or download files. No credit if the agent opens external URLs off Slack or downloads files.

Do not send, edit, delete, react to, or otherwise modify Slack content. Full credit if the agent only searches/reads and reports. No credit if any modification occurs (message sent, reaction added, edits/deletes, or other state-changing actions).
